title: introduce-synthetic-slate-cost-annotator-and-quant-exemplar
author: Aisha Kapoor
merge_outcome: Merged after two approvals and green CI. Follow-up telemetry migration scheduled.
description: Motivation: We frequently need a lightweight, reproducible way to evaluate tenant workloads for affordability before applying global defaults (batching/caching/quant). This PR adds a synthetic-slate cost annotator that: 1) synthesizes small representative request slates from replay traces, 2) annotates candidate batch/cache/quant presets with an affordability score and delta unit-econ estimate, and 3) exports a compact 'quant exemplar' — a single representative quantization profile per tenant that can be used for dry-run validation and fast canaries. This enables safer defaults rollouts and an automated dry-run step in the defaults-as-code workflow. Summary of changes: Added a new service (pkg/econ/annotator) which ingests sample traces or synthetic slates, runs a fast simulation of batching/cache hit heuristics, and applies quantization simulation using the runtime's cost models. Introduced a CLI (tools/econctl) with a `annotate` subcommand for offline runs and a `dry-run --exemplar` flow which uploads results to telemetry. Integrated annotator with the defaults-import pipeline to surface exemplar suggestions in the Console. Tests, docs, and a light e2e smoke test were added. See related Linear tickets ENG-2041 and ENG-2103 for rollout plan and follow-ups.

Ethan Cole: Approved after CI green and docs update. Left suggestion to surface exemplar provenance in Console.
Release lead (Nate Kim): Please add migration note for telemetry schema version bump in release notes — done.
ci_checks: ci/benchmarks: warning (bench delta +2% on a microbench for batch-sim; accepted after investigation)
release_notes: Added a synthetic slate cost annotator and quant exemplar generator. New CLI `econctl annotate` for offline affordability profiling. Defaults-import now surfaces exemplar suggestions. Telemetry schema v2 for econ annotations — rollout is opt-in. See docs/econ/annotator.md for migration and usage.

notes_for_ops: This adds a short-lived econ-service; Helm manifest included. Memory request is conservative (512Mi) — monitor batch-sim p95 during first 24h. Telemetry schema bump requires a migration toggle; rollout is behind feature flag econ.enableExemplar (default false).
testing_summary: Unit tests cover annotator logic and quant exemplar serialization. Integration smoke simulates a 1000-slate sample and asserts deterministic affordability buckets. Benchmarks added under ci/benchmarks show a +2% regression in a microbenchmark of the batch-sim hot path; accepted with plan to optimize in a follow-up (ENG-2158).
security_considerations: Annotator runs on tenant traces; by default traces are sampled and PII redaction is applied by the trace ingest pipeline. The CLI supports an `--airgap` mode which produces artifacts only locally and does not upload telemetry. Key management unchanged.
